$schema-note: One theme preset (design brief 2026-08-27, §4.1). A preset is a complete designed look: two authored palettes, a type map for all four roles, shape and texture and density, a motif default, and the curated option sets from the visual story.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings — the generator writes the RGB triples (brief §3.6). The dark palette is authored value by value; no dark value is derived from its light twin.
$first-class-note: See design/tokens/presets/civic.json: all six styles are first-class, each with one recommended configuration.
label: Broadsheet
summary: The paper of record. The nameplate is the loudest thing on the page and rules do the dividing.
bestFor: Formal programmes, anniversary editions, and events that want the paper-of-record voice.
$palette-words-light: newsprint white, press black, deep ink-blue, warm rule grey, gutter grey, agate grey, margin white, archive grey
$palette-words-dark: late-edition charcoal, warm bone type, lifted ink-blue, smoke-grey rule, banked ink, press-room grey, dim agate grey, muted archive grey
$font-note: Brief §9.4 and §4.1. Broadsheet is the one preset that runs a serif in the mono role: a listings column in a paper is set in agate, not in a typewriter face.
$tokens-note: Preset-level remaps of existing tier 2 and tier 3 tokens. No new property name (brief §3.4).

choices.label: Libre Caslon Display
choices.why: The paper of record founded in the 1820s. It is the canonical masthead voice and the reason the story reads as authority.

choices.label: Libre Baskerville
choices.why: The same paper, founded sixty years later. Its more even colour and open counters keep the authority while reading a shade less antique.

choices.label: Spectral semibold
choices.why: The paper of record that redesigned in this century. It holds the serious register while giving a modern client a masthead that does not look inherited.

choices.label: Full measure
choices.why: Name across the full column width, the nameplate rule under it, edition slug below. The front page of a broadsheet, exactly.

choices.label: Centred with a double rule
choices.why: The ceremonial masthead a paper uses on an anniversary edition, so it stays inside the story while reading more formal.

choices.label: Compact left with a standing edition line
choices.why: The running head on an inside page, which is why it fits inner pages and the nameplate-compact header variant.

choices.label: Ruled programme
choices.why: Hairline rows, times in the agate column. The printed programme page.

choices.label: Agate block
choices.why: The classified and listings page of the same paper, so the density reads as another part of the document rather than a different design.
